summary: Re-tested yard delete flow after main agent migrated deleteYard() to askConfirm/ConfirmDialog. All 3 scenarios pass in the preview iframe: cancel button closes dialog without deleting, backdrop overlay click closes dialog without deleting, and confirm button actually deletes the yard (row disappears, 'Deleted' toast shown, list refreshed). Native window.confirm was NEVER invoked at any point (verified via init-script hook). Grep also confirms zero window.confirm usages remain in AdminPage.jsx. Iteration 3's outstanding bug is fully resolved.
critical_code_review_comments: Minor (carry-over from iteration 3, not blocking): ConfirmDialog's confirm button label is hard-coded to 'Delete' in AdminPage.jsx line 665. If askConfirm is reused for non-destructive actions in the future, consider making the confirm-button label a prop.

Minor (carry-over): No loading/disabled state on confirm-dialog-confirm while the DELETE request is in-flight - a fast double-click could theoretically fire two DELETEs. Consider disabling the button once clicked.
seed_data_creation: Created disposable yard 'TESTDELYard_ITER4' via admin Add form, then deleted it via UI in the confirm-button test. No residual test data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Yard delete bug is fully fixed. All three admin delete flows (users, ceramics, yards) now consistently use the in-page ConfirmDialog with the askConfirm pattern. No window.confirm remains in AdminPage.jsx (verified via grep). If additional destructive-action features are added in the future, they should follow the same askConfirm() pattern.
rca of the issue: N/A - the iteration-3 bug (deleteYard still calling window.confirm) has been resolved by the main agent's fix. deleteYard (lines 334-348) now mirrors deleteUser/deleteCeramic and calls askConfirm() which sets the confirm state and renders <ConfirmDialog data-testid='confirm-dialog'>. Verified in preview environment with an init-script hook that overrode window.confirm to record any call; hook flag remained false across all three flows.
